name: Command Decisions: The Leaders of the Second World War
description: The dictators, prime ministers, generals and admirals of the Second World War, and the conferences and choices that turned on them, from Munich to Potsdam and Nuremberg.

checkpoints.name: Appeasement and the fall of France
checkpoints.note: Neville Chamberlain signs the Munich Agreement with Hitler and Mussolini in 1938, hoping to buy peace. Within a year Hitler's armies are at war, Guderian's tanks lead the sweep through France, de Gaulle refuses defeat from London, and Churchill replaces Chamberlain as Britain's leader. Roosevelt hears from scientists that a bomb may be possible.

checkpoints.name: The war widens
checkpoints.note: Hitler turns on Stalin's Soviet Union, Haile Selassie returns to Ethiopia, and Tojo's government approves Yamamoto's plan to strike the American fleet. Nimitz takes the Pacific command and MacArthur leaves the Philippines, Rommel meets Montgomery in the desert, Zhukov plans the Soviet counterstroke, and Nazi officials at Wannsee plan the murder of Europe's Jews, carried out by Himmler's SS.

checkpoints.name: The tide turns
checkpoints.note: Tito's partisans tie down German divisions, Chiang Kai-shek keeps China in the war, and MacArthur and Nimitz split the Pacific advance. Eisenhower commands the Normandy landings, with Montgomery on the ground and Patton breaking out that summer. Rommel, linked to the plot against Hitler, is forced to kill himself, and Allied delegates at Bretton Woods design the post-war money system.

checkpoints.name: Victory and judgement
checkpoints.note: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin shape the peace at Yalta. Roosevelt dies in April 1945 and Truman inherits the war and the Manhattan Project's bomb. Hitler, Mussolini and Himmler die as their regimes fall, the UN Charter is signed, Truman meets Stalin at Potsdam, and after Hiroshima and Nagasaki Hirohito accepts surrender. The Nuremberg trials judge the surviving Nazi leaders.
